Baby hearts in crises follow up

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
When we interviewed the HOD for the last story they promised that the only Cath Lab in the EC would be up and running by the end of March. On the 27th of March they sent us an email saying we could come do a follow up story as the Lab had arrived. It is nearly the end of June and the Cath Lab is not up and running. Construction on the space where the Lab needs to be installed has not begun due to issues around securing finance from treasury. The only Anaesthetist that can do paediatric heart surgery has been banned from PE provincial by the unions for requesting that they do more surgeries per day and he was accused of racism. The Anaesthetist he trained has gone into private, she was asked to come back and do sessions but after she asked for a contract she has heard nothing back from them for weeks. Neither of these two will speak

Waiting list for Paediatric heart surgery is sitting at over 150 children.
They now have a deal with a private Cath lab, but allowances are significantly less than what they were doing when the Lab was working. The contract was due to end at the end of July, but head of Paediatrics says he has been told that they were allowed 50 patients and they have reached their limit.

Red cross has taken some cases, still trying to confirm how many, but they are back logged and won't take patients previously worked on by another surgeon.






Further information:
Case studies:
Tsepang: Her son is 9 years old, but due to his heart condition he is physically like a 5 year old. He has been operated on before, so Red cross won't take him. Open heart surgery booked for 10th June, but now she has no idea when he will get surgery. Limited communication with her from the hospital

Yullina: Her son Junior 10 months old has been waiting for surgery since 20 March he is in a critical condition. This week he is being transported to a hospital in Cape town to await surgery at Red cross. She doesn't have a date for his surgery yet. I can find a replacement for him or maybe a CT producer can interview the mom? We have cellphone footage of him in hospital
Mom will have to go to CT and live in the hospital until he gets surgery and is well enough to come home.

Request for specialist that I have put in
Rowlene Wagner Deputy Director General for department of Health in EC. She is a straight shooter and knows all the details
Dr Mda is the new head pf Paediatrics for PE, he has agreed and is asking state. Not sure they will let him hey?

Adele won't speak, she seems to have lost all hope. She says there is no point as nothing changed after the previous story :( but i think she wants to be able to do sessions at state and is afraid.

Press Release:


Baby Hearts in Crisis
In the Eastern Cape, there is just one fully functional catheterization lab to service the entire province. But the machine has been broken since October last year and paediatric patients diagnosed with congenital heart disease are being forced to wait for months for treatment. But despite the government’s promises to Carte Blanche in March this year to have the lab up and running, nothing has changed. Now with no surgical staff for paediatric heart surgery as well – heart patients in the province face a severe crisis.
Producer: Tarryn Crossman
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:00 Voice over In March this year we did a story on the states lack of life saving cardiology services in the Eastern Cape as the only catheterization laboritary that services 6 million people had not been operational since October 2018. A cath lab is a specialised theatre used for the diagnosis of heart disease and allows for heart saving surgeries to be performed through a catheter like stems, angioplasties or valve replacements
2 00:30 Macfarlane Link That was 4 months ago, but nothing has changed. The situation is still as dire as explained by Cardiology specialist Dr. Pepeta in March, especially for children born with congenital heart disease
3 00:42 Dr Pepete and Devi interview Pepete: Yeah a new born with a blocked vessel doesn’t have a couple of months, they have a day or 2

Devi: what happens to those children?

Pepete: they get admitted in the ward they get medication and nothing is done they get infections. Iof they are lucky they will get to another central hospital. They go there but they may not always get in so again they will die.
4 01:05 Macfarlane link For Paediatric patients the situation has gravely deteriorated, Not only is there no Cath Lab, but due to staffing issues there has been no paediatric heart surgery on and off since February this year.

5 01:17 Voice over The waiting list for pediatrics to gets Caths done is 94 children and the waiting list for
surgery is over 100 children. One of the children on this waiting list is Yullin Sukman sons Junior. He was diagnosed with a severe congenital heart disease. He is now 10 months old and has spent almost his entire life in hospital.
6 01:38 Yullin Sakman Its painful to have a child who have a heart problem, sometimes he w as turning blue sometimes he was fine, sometimes he wants to eat and sometimes he doesn’t want to eat. I have to look after my child 24/7
7 01:52 Voice over
In March Yullin was told that Junior needed urgent diagnostic caths, but the facilities were not available so he would simply have to wait. Dr Mahlubandile Nxele is a state Pediatric cardiologist at PE Provincial hospital
8 02:08 Dr. Nxele Junior mother shouldn’t have been in hospital for that long and if the cath labs were working and the suyrgey was going on he would have gotten his surgery not wait for this long.
9 02:25 Voice over Rolene Wagner was appointed at the Acting Deputy Director general for the Eastern Cape department of Health in February this year.
10 02:33 Interview with Rolene and Macfarlane Macfarlane: Yullin has been sitting in hospital for 10 months, what went wrong there? So much more coulve been done.

Rolene: I think the difficult thing that faces any country and not in South Africa is that theres always a demand for care and with limited resources its not possible to do every child exactly when it is required But we do our best when we try and do the child within that window of opportunity when the operation can be done.
11 02:56 Video of Junior
12 03:00 Yullin They are saying we have to wait for the doctor to do it and every time they told me they will do it on Monday and when the time come on Monday they say I have to wait another week. They say everytime its emergency, its emergency, its emergencis but I think myself junior is also emergency so they have to help him also q
13 03:26 Voice over In an attempt to alleviate the crises the department has put a deal in place with Netcare to use their private cath Labs. But again access is limited.
14 03:36 Rolene: when we realised now that we are going to be facing a longer period and that these emergencies are going to occur that is when we entered and arrangement and nNetcare was the service provider that met the requirements
Macfarlane: Are you then seeing as many kids in the private sector as you would be seeing had this cath lab be up and running?
Rolene: Well when our cath lab is up and running we are able to utilise it between Monday to Friday at present we are only able to do 2 slates per week so obviously we are not seeing as many had we had our own lab up and running
15 04:06 Voice over Lungile Mokhoele Was born with Congenital heart disease, which requires regular treatment. He is now 9 years old. After Waiting for diagnostic Caths for 8 months his condition has greatly deteriorated
16 04:22 Dr Nxele He has Palminary hypertention which means the pressure is high on the lungs, surgery need to be done as soon as possible. If its left unattended then it goes onto you know irrevesable but like im saying lungile needs surgery like today or tomorroe so he will be one of the patients that we have to push in when we have a chance to start with suyrgery because if we wait too long we might miss the boat.
16 04:49 Voice over As the department of health takes months to try find solutions to this crises the ones suffering are the patients and at the coal face are the parents like Lungil’s mom Tsepang Mokhoela
17 05:02 Tsepang and Macfarlane interview Tsepang: He’s smart but he doesn’t grow. Kids his age are bigger than him, he looks like hes 6 or 7 years old but hes very clever and hes smarter than other kids, its just this condition he has.
Macfarlane: Can he play with other kids?
Tsepan: He can but he gets tired easily, so the doctor said he mustn’t run until he gets surgery. I cant leave him and go anywhere, if I leave him he cries and when I come back hes not okay and I have to take him to the hospital.
18 05:43 Voice over On the 27 th of March we received this email from the Department of Health proudly inviting us to come and do a follow up story, as the Cath Lab had arrived. It is now July and The Cath Lab Equipment is still sitting in these crates at the PE Provincial hospital waiting to be installed.
19 05:59 Rolene and macfarlane interview Macfaralne: What has happened?
Rolene: Part of being able to install and commission the equipment required us to make adjustment to the infrustracutre and it ook longer than expected because the insuring that we comply with the regulations that govern the supply management and procurement it take long
20 06:18 Voice over While the installation of the Cath Lab continues to be delayed the cost to state to access Netcares Cath Labs is 100000 per month. In an under resourced state health care system this is a massive expense to the tax payer that is going to continue until the Catherization Lab in PE provincial hospital is fully operational
21 06:39 Macfarlane and Rolene Rolene: So we have met with our service providers and we will be handing site over to them next Monday on the 15th of July they then anticipate that it will take 5 weeks to complete the enabling works and we hand over to the second provoder who will do installation of the cath lab and that will take 3 weeks so our predicted completion date and hand over to us is on the 9th of September. Now that we know that the new date is going ot be on the 9th of septemeber we are goingto have to go back to the private sector now and look at when their cath l;abs will be available for us to utilise in the sam e way that we have done before.
22 07:12 Voice over The projected time frame for an end to this Cath Lab crisis is 11 months after it all begun. With regards to Pediatric surgeries though, a Private Pediatric cardiology surgeon and Anesthetist have been contracted to provide limited access to pediatric heart surgery after 6 months of interrupted services
23 07:33 Macfarlane and Rolene Macfarlane: So Rolene when will then these surgeries officially begin?
Rolene: Our proffessors have scheduled the first the resumption for Thursday 11 of July.
24 07:42 Link Even though Pediatric surgery will begin again there will only be 2 surgeries per week and with such a massive backlog it will takes months to catch up
25 07:52 Rolene Rolene: so I put that question to the clinitians and they believe that if we can get the cath lab up and running restore the surgeries they will do their best to try and eliminate that back log that we have at the moment. Again each case will be dealt with depending on its complexity.
26 08:09 Voice over After finally receiving his diagnostic cath’s Junior was transferred to Red cross hospital, but his mom has still not been given a date for his surgery
27 08:18 Yullin I just want the doctors to do the operation so that we can go home and be a family at home I want him to be fine that’s all
28 08:29 Voice over Even though Dr Nxele was clear that Lungile needed immediate surgery, his mom has heard nothing from the cardiology clinic
29 08:38 Tsepang Im concerned, I want my child to get the help that he needs beause his life is in the hands of the surgery. I would feel better if I knew what was happeneing. Right now his life is just on hold
